nodes.label: Platform Custodial Stellar Account (PLATFORM_PAYTO + PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Single custodial pool that receives all user top-ups and signs every on-chain contributor payout; must be funded to cover payouts plus fees. If PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY is unset, payouts are recorded as unpaid (txid null).

nodes.label: Horizon Endpoint (confirm top-ups + send payouts)
nodes.rationale: Horizon is Stellar's classic REST API layer; the registry uses it (https://horizon-testnet.stellar.org by default) to confirm XLM deposit transactions on-chain and to submit contributor payout payments, as opposed to the Soroban RPC used for smart-contract calls.

nodes.label: Bore Tunnel SSH Exposure (dial-out, no inbound ports)
nodes.rationale: The bore tunnel runs inside each sandbox and dials out, so contributors open no inbound ports and install nothing; TUNNEL_MODE=local skips bore for same-machine SSH to 127.0.0.1. Public bore.pub is best-effort — run your own BORE_SERVER beyond demos.

nodes.label: Friendbot Testnet Funding
nodes.rationale: Friendbot is Stellar's testnet faucet: hitting https://friendbot.stellar.org/?addr=<G...> funds a new testnet account with free XLM, which is how all Tendril test accounts are funded.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres (money state: wallets, topups, charges, payouts)
In-Memory Nodes/Leases (deliberate non-persistence)
nodes.rationale: Nodes and leases live in registry memory on purpose: a restart drops live sessions (their sockets die anyway) but keeps Postgres out of the heartbeat/watchdog hot path. For HA, persist and externalize (e.g. socket.io Redis adapter + shared store).
